title: Feature start seeds every gate as pending, and bee gate records who approved and why
action: Make a run enter awaiting-approval on its own, and make an approval say who and why (per D1, D2, D3). Two halves. FIRST: `bee state start-feature` must seed every gate on the new record with state "pending" instead of a bare approved:false — the attachment points are the default_gates() calls in state_group/policy.rs near lines 390 and 506. After this, starting a feature is what puts the run into awaiting-approval; nobody types it. SECOND: `bee state gate` gains three optional flags — --actor ("user" or "auto", defaulting to "user"), --bypass-level (one of off, normal, full, total), and --reason (free text) — and writes them onto the entry with the current timestamp. The flag allowlist to extend is in run_gate_body in state_group/set_gate.rs (search for the accepted-flags list containing "name", "merge", "approved", "lane", "no-lane", "owner", near line 549); the write itself is near line 700-710. --approved false continues to stamp gate_revoked_at exactly as today (search set_gate.rs for `gate_revoked_at`, near line 690) and additionally sets state "rejected". Per D2 an auto-approval is REQUIRED to carry --actor auto plus --bypass-level and --reason: refuse an --actor auto call that omits either, so a bypassed run can never be less traceable than a stopped one. If the CLI help or registry payload is generated from a declaration rather than hand-written, regenerate it in the same cell so the shipped surface matches.

truths: bee state start-feature leaves every gate on the new record with state pending
bee gate --approved true --actor user records state approved, actor user, and a timestamp
bee gate --approved true --actor auto --bypass-level normal --reason X records all three on the entry
bee gate --actor auto without --bypass-level or without --reason refuses and writes nothing
bee gate --approved false still stamps gate_revoked_at and sets state rejected

deviations: The cell's action text points at default_gates() in state_group/policy.rs (lines 390/506) as the seam that seeds pending gates at start-feature. Confirmed (per trun-1's own note, reread against the code) that default_gates() only resets the PROJECTED .bee/state.json approved_gates boolean, never the D3 record's state/actor/at/reason/bypass_level fields. The real seam is default_gate_entry() in workflow_store/record.rs, already landed by trun-1: ensure_workflow_record_for_feature's primary path (run_start_feature) passes gates: None, so a brand-new record already gets state:"pending" on every gate for free. Left policy.rs untouched; added a_new_feature_record_seeds_every_gate_as_pending (state_group/tests.rs) as the proof instead of a code change.

The actor/at/reason/bypass_level trace never reaches gates_patch_from_record (workflow_store/handoff.rs) or write_through_projection (state_group/ledger.rs) — both are outside this cell's declared files. Instead, run_gate_body issues a second, still-lock-held update_workflow_assuming_lock_with patch (using only functions already imported into set_gate.rs) that stamps the trace onto exactly the touched gate name(s) after the existing write_through_projection call lands approved/state. This avoids widening the cell's file scope while keeping the write inside the same workflow lock.

The action text says to regenerate the CLI help/registry payload if it is generated from a declaration. packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/generated/registry_payload.json is NOT in this cell's declared files, and its generator (scripts/export_registry_payload.mjs, per its own regen comment) no longer exists in this repo (Node runtime removed, per src/main.rs's own header). No cli_shape/registry validation gates a native verb before try_native — run_gate's own keys_known allowlist (extended in this cell) is what the real CLI enforces, so behavior is correct and fully tested without this file. The registry_payload.json entry for `state gate` still lacks --actor/--bypass-level/--reason in its documented parameters (bee --help --json), which is a real but doc-only gap — flagging it for the orchestrator rather than hand-editing a 184KB generated file outside this cell's scope.
